research interests. The Santa Clara Valley is one of the least understood areas in California from an archaeological perspective. Only with the advent of the environmental impact report process has ther been consistent archaeological study in the area. No archaeological sites have been located in the project areas addressed in this report. * This is more a factor of inadequate investigation than lack of resources. The rapid urban development of San Jose has destroyed or obsured many of the archaeological resources of the Santa Clara Valley. Some have managed to survive, often under the foundations of older portions of the city. Important among these was the recent discovery of the ancient village site in the vicinity of the new Holiday Inn in downtown San Jose. Other studies in this area, including the environmental impact report of the Guadalupe Park Plaza, have suggested the possible survival of archaeological resources in the urban heart (Edwards 1974).
* The potential historic and archaeological impacts of the San Antonio Plaza Redevelopment Project have been evaluated in the EIR prepared for that project. Archaeological field work is currently in progress in the San Antonio Redevelopment site.
